name: Falciparum malaria, carried by Anopheles mosquitoes
_doc: As trypanosomiasis.json. Host 'people': annual_loss_at_full_challenge is an excess death rate per year for each demography band (children, working_age, elderly), added to baseline mortality and scaled by the disease burden the nation has not yet removed.

challenge_envelope.source: Temperature: Mordecai et al. 2013 Ecology Letters 16:22, abstract via USGS (pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70125667): 'predicts optimal malaria transmission at 25 C' and 'transmission decreases dramatically at temperatures > 28 C'; the 17 to 34 C limits are quoted from Ryan et al. (arXiv 1407.7612): 'temperatures between 17-34 C (Mordecai et al. 2013)'. The 22 to 28 C optimum band is centred on the 25 C optimum (+-3 C, upper edge at the 28 C decline), derived. Rainfall: Smith et al. 2020 (Nature Communications, PMC7455692, opened) apply Craig et al. 1999 as a monthly threshold of '80 mm month-1' and an 18 C monthly minimum. Derived annual edges: 80 mm in every month is 960 mm, taken as the 1000 mm lower optimum edge; 80 mm in only the wettest five months is 400 mm, the tolerated lower edge (five months is an assumption). Upper edges: Papua New Guinea has malaria-endemic lowlands with rainfall 'reaching up to 4000 mm annually in the southwestern and northern coastal regions', Madang at 3394 mm a year (PMC4825189, opened), which supports the 4000 mm optimum edge; the 6000 mm tolerated edge is above anything opened and is a stand-in.

hosts.people.source: Wikipedia, History of malaria (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_malaria, opened): 'Faragher gave a tentative estimate of about 4-5% of deaths being caused by malaria' over history. With a crude death rate of 30-40 per 1,000 a year (my assumption for an agrarian population), that is 1.2 to 2 malaria deaths per 1,000 people a year averaged over a country. The file's rates (0.015 children, 0.002 working age, 0.004 elderly) give about 7 per 1,000 for a population a third children at full challenge, so a country with a fifth to a third of its people at full challenge matches. WHO malaria fact sheet (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/malaria, opened): 75% of African-region deaths are under five, 2.2 deaths per 1,000 cases in 2024 with modern treatment. Ballpark, not a register.
